A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LIVR and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C. Matching content across relocation and renumbering supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original single-task and multi-task experiments, Mirage comparisons, ablations, and latent-token analyses in Sections 4.3–4.5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds LIVR results on external reasoning benchmarks, larger-model comparisons, and another control. Tables 3–4 distinguish its original LIVR results from externally reported comparator scores.

M1.justification: The learned latent tokens, visual bottleneck attention mask, two-stage training, and answer-token NLL objective remain unchanged. Revised explanations and applications to additional backbones do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 adds SAT-32k and Visual-CoT training, with evaluation on SAT Val, RoboSpatial, MMVP, V*, and additional BLINK coverage including relative depth, multi-view reasoning, spatial relations, and IQ tests. The original nine tasks and VSP remain; removing the Mirage–Jigsaw comparison does not remove Jigsaw coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds reported comparisons against ViGoRL, vanilla GRPO, text-CoT SFT+GRPO, PAPO, Vision-R1, PixelReasoner, and LVR, plus 7B Mirage variants with text-CoT and RL. Most new comparator scores are explicitly taken from prior reports. Conversely, Mirage is removed from the Jigsaw comparison while remaining in VSP.

E3.justification: The original single-task and multi-task protocols remain unchanged. Added protocols include Qwen2.5-VL-7B experiments, SAT-32k and Visual-CoT training with intermediate supervision removed for LIVR, specified BLINK subsets and RoboSpatial splits, and a duplicate-image control trained with two-stage masking.

E4.justification: v2 adds an explicit synthetic-to-real generalization study using SAT training and real-image spatial evaluations, substantially extending the tested generalization conditions. Table 5 also adds a control testing whether duplicated image tokens with two-stage masking can substitute for learned latents. Existing ablations, attention analyses, and t-SNE evidence are retained; t-SNE merely moves to Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose a fixed random seed of 42 in Appendix B and report point accuracies without repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional results do not change this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and retained ablation values are unchanged. New comparisons report, for example, SAT accuracy of 85.6 versus ViGoRL's 62.9, MMVP accuracy of 75.3 versus LVR's 71.7, and BLINK-5 accuracy of 54.28 versus LVR's 55.37. v2 also adds 7B VSP accuracy of 77.50 and the masked duplicate-image results, while removing the Jigsaw comparison of LIVR 68.00 versus Mirage 48.60. These are added or removed settings, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, training objective, and relative-reflectance construction are unchanged. Removing an extra closing parenthesis in the LMM expression is a typesetting correction; no substantive definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The core contribution of learning visual latents without intermediate supervision remains. The abstract and introduction replace the broad state-of-the-art claim with a qualified claim of competitiveness or superiority against prior reasoning methods, and explicitly distinguish controlled data-matched evidence from external benchmark comparisons.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the added spatial experiments as evidence of synthetic-to-real and out-of-distribution generalization. Section 6 also clarifies that task-relevant attention does not reveal precisely what each latent encodes. Existing attention and t-SNE interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link in the abstract, providing an additional access point without establishing code or data availability within the PDFs. Appendix A's construction details and prompts, and Appendix B's optimization, hardware, and training disclosures, are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven references, including ViGoRL, PixelReasoner, PAPO, DeepEyes, SAT, RoboSpatial, and DeepSeekMath. It expands discussion of region-based recycling and generated intermediates while retaining the central positioning against predefined intermediate supervision. LVR and Mirage were already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, substantial related-work passages, method explanations, conclusion, and limitations are rewritten. The evaluation narrative is reorganized into data-matched experiments and prior-method comparisons, and the t-SNE discussion moves to Appendix C. These changes substantially revise the paper's organization and exposition.

P2.justification: v2 adds two compact comparison tables, extends the design-ablation table by one row, refreshes Figure 1, and relocates figures, including moving Figure 4 to the appendix. The method diagram, attention visualizations, t-SNE plot, dataset illustrations, and overall two-column format are preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the empirical case with relevant prior-method comparisons, transfer evaluations, and an additional masking control, while replacing v1's broad state-of-the-art claim with a better-qualified competitive claim. The improvement is bounded: many new comparator scores come from prior reports, detailed training schedules for the new SAT/Visual-CoT experiments are not supplied, and the Mirage–Jigsaw comparison is removed. The original controlled evidence remains intact.
